newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Former Filipina WW2 sex slave dies of heart attack.
newsitem.headline: Former Filipina WW2 sex slave dies of heart attack.

text.p: The first Filipina to publicly reveal the horrors she suffered as a sex slave to Japanese forces during World War Two has died of a heart attack, a group of war-time "comfort women" said on Tuesday.
Maria Rosa Henson, 69, died on Monday a week after she was taken to a hospital with pneumonia, the group Lila Filipina said.

Popularly called "Lola (Grandma) Rosa," Henson went public in 1992 and said she was among many young Filipinas forced into battlefield brothels for Japanese soldiers during their more than three years' occupation of the Philippines.
Her example encouraged other former "sex slaves," some in their 70s and 80s, to also come out and relate their ordeals.

"At least, I was able to help the young generation learn what happened so that it will never be repeated," Lila Filipina coordinator Nelia Sancho quoted Henson as saying after she was taken to hospital.
In 1996, Henson, along with six other Filipinas, received an $18,500 compensation from a private Japanese welfare fund and a letter of apology from Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
Since Henson broke her 50-year silence to reveal her war-time ordeal, 180 other Filipino "comfort women" have come out in public. Six of them have since died.
Forty-six, including Henson, have a pending lawsuit before a Tokyo court for legal compensation from the Japanese government.

Henson said she was only 14 when three Japanese soldiers raped her near her Manila home in 1942. She was later taken to a garrison where soldiers, sometimes as many as 12 at a time, would take turns raping her day and night, she said.
Guerrillas rescued her after nine months.
Historians estimate as many as 200,000 Asian women, most of them from Korea, were forced into sexual slavery in Japanese military brothels during the war.
